correctness.rationale: For all m,d>0, q is C1 and has derivative sign equal, after the second pulse, to the explicit concave quadratic F. Its vertex and discriminant prove precisely m>C(d) for a second strict maximum when d>2; d<2 and d=2 are handled separately; the fold equality has no second strict maximum. Log differentiation shows the unique maximum of C at 2sqrt(2). Elementary rational and exponential inequalities prove the 2,1,2 example without relying on numeric sampling. The standalone program confirms 3999 nondegenerate random cases and checks the example; finite checks are not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: Three-reservoir Nash routing of multiple distinct rainfall-excess events is a standard motivated hydrologic construction, and whether the outlet exhibits one or two temporal maxima is a directly meaningful structural observable. The theorem provides the exact necessary-and-sufficient all-parameter phase boundary and reveals that extra temporal separation can erase then restore a second distinct peak for the same storm-volume ratio. The equal-storm case misses this nonmonotone phenomenon, so the extension is not only a numeric parameter update. No downstream applied forecast or general nonlinear flood claim is asserted.
